overview: Black plays the reversed Grob, 1...g5, offering the g-pawn. White's best is 2.d4 Bg7 3.Nc3 d6 4.h4 or 3.Bxg5, taking the pawn with a big centre. Black fianchettoes the bishop and relies on pressure on d4 and the long diagonal for compensation. It is a surprise weapon that gives White a pawn and a good centre.

white_ideas.idea: Take the pawn on g5 with Bxg5 or h4, and build the e4/d4 centre.
Develop and exploit the weakened kingside while avoiding the long diagonal pressure.

black_ideas.idea: Fianchetto the bishop to g7 and hit d4 and the long diagonal for compensation.
Play for ...c5 and ...d6 undermining the centre.

typical_structures.structure: White big centre on d4/e4 with a pawn up; Black fianchetto with a weakened kingside.

character.notes: Black's risk-taking surprise; White has clear plans and Black takes most of the risk.

gambit.notes: 2.d4 Bg7 3.Nc3 and Bxg5/h4 wins the g5 pawn; Black gets some compensation.

soundness.notes: Considered unsound; White gets a clear edge with simple play.

structure.notes: White d4/e4 against Black's fianchetto and no fixed centre.

approach.notes: A reversed Grob used almost only for surprise.

level.notes: Dubious, so never Beginner; few lines but traps need to be known.

sublines_that_differ.name: Langhorst Gambit
sublines_that_differ.how: Black offers a second pawn for pressure on the long diagonal.

character.reason: An aggressive flank gambit with risk for Black, though White's path is clear.

gambit.reason: Black offers the g-pawn that White can keep.

structure.reason: White gets a centre while Black fianchettoes, undecided structure.

level.reason: A dubious line is never Beginner; traps matter more than plans.

plans.reason: The g7 bishop is Black's main source of counterplay.
